summary: cryptostock ships remote-shell backdoor, private-key harvester, and ETH wallet drainer
details: On require(), index.js starts a polling C2 client that fetches shell commands from https://badai.run.place/cekapppiapi.php, executes them via child_process.exec, and POSTs AES-256-ECB-encrypted output to https://badai.run.place/fallback.php. In parallel, the module walks SSH, TLS, and Ethereum keystore directories (/root/.ssh, /home/*/.ssh, /opt/wallet-keys, /etc/ssl/private, ~/.ethereum/keystore, /var/lib/ethereum/keystore, /mnt/crypto/wallets), reads *.pem, *.key, UTC--*, and keystore files, captures ETH_PRIVATE_KEY from the environment, and uploads matches to the same C2. For every recovered 64-hex private key, the code uses Web3 against mainnet.infura.io to sign and broadcast a transaction sending the account's full ETH balance to a hardcoded attacker address. Sensitive strings (host, endpoints, paths, keyword filters) are stored as a base64 string array and decoded at runtime; a header comment self-identifies the code as 'integrated StealthC2 from Badnew.py'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
